match.reason: No bank point teaches the wave equation v = fλ at Stage 5 depth: the closest, phys-waves-their-properties, is a Victorian senior Physics card that adds period and transverse waves, which would need removing rather than small adjusting, and sci-parts-wave only defines the parts of a wave without the equation.

draft.title: The wave equation
card: the distance from one point on a wave to the same point on the next wave, such as crest to crest. It is measured in metres (m).
the number of waves that pass a point each second. It is measured in hertz (Hz), where 1 Hz is one wave per second.
the maximum distance a particle moves from its rest position. A bigger amplitude means the wave carries more energy.
how fast the wave moves, in metres per second (m/s). Wave speed = frequency × wavelength, or \(v = f \lambda\).
draft.remember: Speed = frequency × wavelength. Amplitude is about energy, not speed.

a.q: A wave has a frequency of 5 Hz and a wavelength of 3 m. What is its speed?
a.why: Wave speed = frequency × wavelength = 5 × 3 = 15 m/s. Adding the two numbers (8) is tempting, but the equation multiplies them.

b.q: Kai makes waves on a rope. The waves travel at 6 m/s and have a wavelength of 2 m. How many waves pass a point on the rope each second?
b.why: Frequency = speed ÷ wavelength = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 Hz, so 3 waves pass each second. Multiplying 6 × 2 gives 12, but that treats speed like a frequency instead of rearranging the equation.
b.clue: Rearrange the equation to find frequency.

wants.brief: A transverse wave drawn as a smooth sine curve along a horizontal rest line. Label one crest, one trough, the wavelength as the distance from crest to the next crest, and the amplitude as the height from the rest line to a crest.
wants.why: It lets students see wavelength and amplitude as distances on a wave.
